User reported all V3 circuits had a Bad Object Record error and supplied a Proteus-saved NE555 file that no longer had the error. Comparing generated V3 NE555 with the saved oracle showed ROOT.CDB was unchanged and terminal/WIRE object records were byte-compatible. The saved ROOT.DSN object chunk was exactly the generated object chunk plus one final FF byte. Root cause: the catalogue emitter checked only whether the object chunk ended with FF, but the last component packet can naturally end in FF binary data; the stream still needs an explicit final FF terminator. The safe invariant for this catalogue route is a double-FF ROOT.DSN object-stream ending.
